nodes.name: Patient-6
nodes.summary:
Patient-6 (born February 2, 1970; case number URO-2026-0006) presented with pollakiuria and an elevated total PSA level of 16.7 ng/ml. An mpMRI of the prostate revealed a PI-RADS score of 5, and a core needle biopsy involving 12 prostate core biopsies confirmed an adenocarcinoma of the prostate with a Gleason score of 4+3=7 (ISUP 3), staged as cT2b cN0 cM0. An interdisciplinary tumor board conference on December 20, 2026, recommended primary radiotherapy plus ADT (IMRT + Goserelin) as an alternative to radical prostatectomy. On January 8, 2027, the patient presented at the Klinik für Onkologie und Hämatologie at Klinikum Berlin under the care of Dr. med. Arzt-2, where androgen deprivation therapy was initiated with a Goserelin 3-month depot, with a current PSA level of 13.5 ng/ml and an ECOG performance status of 0. On February 4, 2027, Patient-6 was evaluated following external beam radiotherapy (IMRT 76 Gy to the prostate) and ongoing ADT, with a PSA level of 7.6 ng/ml.
Patient-6 underwent routine laboratory surveillance and follow-up at the Urologische Klinik, Klinikum Berlin on August 1, 2030.
Patient-6 was under the care and follow-up of Dr. med. Arzt-1 on August 1, 2030.

nodes.name: Prostatakarzinom
nodes.summary:
Patient-6 is diagnosed with C61 Prostatakarzinom, staged as cT2b cN0 cM0 with Gleason 4+3=7 (ISUP 3), confirmed by histological examination showing adenocarcinoma of the prostate. Symptoms include pollakisurie while maintaining a good general condition with an ECOG performance status of 0. Treatment comprises primary external beam radiotherapy (IMRT 76 Gy) plus androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with Goserelin. Routine follow-up evaluations through June 20, 2028, show a favorable therapeutic response with declining and stable PSA levels reaching 0,4 ng/ml and no evidence of disease progression.
